statement

Both headline figures rest on four people, the intravenous reference is described in a separate five-person study without saying who provided it, and no confidence interval appears anywhere in either paper. change: Review and adjudication, ketamine round: the absorption wording is the abstract's and the results' (second reader 224, checked at Clements 1982 pp. 539-540); 'found twice by different groups' qualified, because the 1982 oral condition was a solution and the 2003 one a swallowed tablet; the 2016 review's attachment of the 93% figure to a much larger intramuscular amount brought into the statement; the unreproducible printed time to peak for the swallowed tablet named.

grade.domains.inconsistency.note

The two intravenous half-lives (186 minutes and about 120 minutes) differ by about an hour, which the papers do not reconcile; the amounts, assays and samples differ, and the review's range of 2 to 4 hours brackets both.

The two intravenous half-lives (186 minutes and about 120 minutes) differ by about an hour, which the papers do not reconcile; the amounts, assays, samples and sampling periods differ, and the review's range of 2 to 4 hours brackets both. The 1982 paper itself shows that a shorter sampling period gives a much shorter apparent half-life from its own data (card sc_clements_1982), so the two figures are not measured in the same way.

A 2024 meta-analysis that pooled the published peak coordinates of 33 functional-imaging studies in 628 healthy volunteers, and whose confidence the editors rate critically low, found only two clusters that survived correction for multiple testing, each resting on part of the 395 people in the two analyses that produced results rather than on all 628:
statement
across all 23 task studies together nothing was significant and no decrease was found in any analysis (Ait Bentaleb et al., 2024).

across all 23 task studies together nothing was significant in either direction, and no decrease is reported in any of the three analyses, which the review states outright for the pooled task analysis and which is what its table shows for the other two (Ait Bentaleb et al., 2024). Two things sit beside this. In the same Zurich laboratory the equimolar (R)-form moved the other way, lowering glucose metabolism significantly in two regions (Vollenweider et al., 1997a; the figures are on card sc_vollenweider_1997a), so the direction given here is that of racemic and (S)-ketamine. statement
